question: Do these three black-box LLM distillation methods exist as named published techniques, and what is each in one sentence: (1) Proxy-KD - train a small proxy model to imitate a black-box teacher from text+scores, then distill the student from the proxy with soft labels; (2) ROPD - rubric-based on-policy distillation scoring student outputs against structured rubrics; (3) KED - knowledge explaining distillation where the teacher provides explanations as auxiliary supervision. Give arxiv IDs or URLs where possible.
answer:
Yes, all three of these black-box distillation methods exist as named, published techniques.

Proxy-KD introduces a white-box proxy model between a student and a black-box teacher to align with the teacher's capabilities, allowing the student to train using soft labels and KL divergence from the proxy [1][2][3]. The paper can be found at arXiv:2401.07013 [3].

ROPD (Rubric-based On-policy Distillation) is a framework that induces prompt-specific rubrics by contrasting teacher and student outputs, then uses those rubrics to score student rollouts for on-policy optimization [4][5][6]. It is detailed at arXiv:2605.07396 [4][6].

KED (Knowledge Explaining Distillation) uses "superfeature-explaining teachers" to provide both soft predictions and auxiliary explanations as supervision for the student model [7]. It is documented in an OpenReview submission available at https://openreview.net/pdf?id=3Y6gc7sesn [7].
